chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Hamza ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We guided him to the two paths' [90:10]. He said: 'The path of good and the path of evil.'

key_terms.الشَّرِّ: Evil, wickedness — the path of moral corruption
key_terms.النَّجْدَيْنِ: The two paths/ways — from najd meaning an elevated plateau or prominent road; the dual form. In this hadith interpreted as the path of good and the path of evil
key_terms.الْخَيْرِ: Good, goodness, virtue — the path of moral uprightness

ai.seo_question: What do 'the two paths' (al-najdayn) mean in Quran 90:10 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides an authoritative Quranic interpretation, explaining that the 'two paths' mentioned in Surah al-Balad (90:10) refer to the path of good and the path of evil. This commentary reflects the Shia tradition of seeking Quranic exegesis from the Imams, who are considered the authoritative interpreters of the Book of God. The verse's original audience understood al-najdayn as the two prominent high roads or elevated paths — here the Imam interprets this as a moral and spiritual dichotomy ingrained in human nature.
